paper.title: Optimal Best Markovian Arm Identification with Fixed Confidence

settings.name_in_paper: Best Markovian arm identification with fixed confidence, one-parameter family of Markov chains (lower bound)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Rested Markovian arms (environment markovian) are out of scope from ontology v0.5.
unmapped: Each arm is a rested irreducible finite-state Markov chain from a one-parameter family; only the arm played evolves
Learner observes rewards f(X_n) of the hidden chain; best arm = highest stationary mean
Family satisfies irreducibility, common support of transitions and of initial distributions
settings.definition_quote: There are $K$ Markovian arms with parameters $\btheta = (\theta_1, \ldots, \theta_K) \in \Theta^K$, and each arm $a$ evolves as a Markov chain with parameter $\theta_a$ ... Our goal is to identify $a^* (\btheta)$ with probability at least $1-\delta$ using as few samples as possible.

settings.name_in_paper: Best Markovian arm identification with fixed confidence, one-parameter exponential family of Markov chains
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Rested Markovian arms (environment markovian) are out of scope from ontology v0.5.
unmapped: Arms are rested Markov chains from the exponential family of stochastic matrices generated by a known generator P and reward function f (conditions on S_M, S_m irreducibility and reachability)
The learner knows the generator P and f (constant C(P,f) used in the stopping threshold)
settings.definition_quote: we instantiate the abstract one-parameter family of Markov chains from Section 2.1, with the one-parameter exponential family of Markov chains ... $P_\theta (x, y) = \frac{v_\theta (y)}{v_\theta (x)} e^{\theta \phi (y) - A (\theta)} P (x, y)$

symbols.T_star: Markovian characteristic time: T*(theta)^{-1} = sup_w inf_{lambda in Alt(theta)} sum_a w_a D(theta_a || lambda_a), with D the KL divergence rate between Markov chains

conditions: delta-PC sampling strategies (with E[tau_delta] finite for all instances)
family satisfies irreducibility, common transition support and common initial-distribution support
nonconstant reward function f on finite state space

source.label: thm:lower-bound
source.quote: Fix $\delta \in (0, 1)$, let $f:S \to \Real{}$ be a nonconstant reward function, let $\calA_\delta$ be a $\delta$-PC sampling strategy, and fix a parameter configuration $\btheta \in \bTheta$. Then $T^* (\btheta) \le \liminf_{\delta \to 0} \frac{\Etheta [\tau_\delta]}{\log \frac{1}{\delta}}$

results.notes: Asymptotic lower bound on expected stopping time; T_star uses KL divergence rates, generalising Garivier-Kaufmann.

symbols.T_star: Markovian characteristic time defined via KL divergence rates
symbols.alpha_TaS: convergence parameter alpha of the Chernoff stopping threshold beta(t)=2 log(D t^alpha/delta)

tuning: threshold beta_{alpha,delta}(t) = 2 log(D t^alpha / delta), D = 2 alpha K C^2/(alpha-1)

source.label: thm:upper-bound
source.quote: Let $\btheta \in \bTheta$, and $\alpha \in (1, e/4]$. The $(\alpha, \delta)$-Track-and-Stop strategy, denoted here by $\calA_{\delta}$, has its asymptotic expected sample complexity upper bounded by, $\limsup_{\delta \to 0} \frac{\E_\btheta^{\calA_\delta} [\tau_{\alpha, \delta}]}{\log \frac{1}{\delta}} \le 4 \alpha T^* (\btheta)$.

results.notes: Within factor 4*alpha of the lower bound of Theorem 1.

source.label: prop:PC
source.quote: Let $\delta \in (0, 1)$, and $\alpha \in (1, e/4]$. The $(\alpha, \delta)$-Track-and-Stop strategy is $\delta$-PC.

results.notes: delta-PC: misidentification probability at most delta for all instances, and finite expected stopping time.
